purpose: Research-only observations used to choose refFlowCfs/refSpeedMph. These are not read directly by the production app.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Late Spring on the Klickitat - 1040 cfs' (Thomas O'Keefe, Jun 2, 2026)
observations.notes: Packrafts, overnight trip Leidl to Ice House. Source: 'approximately a six-hour float, including a few fishing stops' and 'total float time ... less than six hours, including all of our fishing stops'. 360 is an upper bound. The stop time is not stated. The flow is the reporter's figure, and the USGS daily mean for 2026-06-02 is also 1040 (provisional). Distance is the catalog section length, not the reporter's figure. Batch 1 re-read (2026-10-25): the clock times in the report conflict with the stated total. They were on the water 'shortly after noon' and reached camp above the Little Klickitat confluence 'a little before 4 p.m.' (about 4 h, roughly 11-12 of 15.8 mi, ~3 mph with stops). Then 'back on the water by 10 a.m.' and 'reached Ice House by 4 p.m.' (6 h for the last ~4-5 mi, unless camp breaks are included). Treat this as low-confidence and use it only as a lower bound on speed.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Klickitat High Water Trip - 4600 cfs' (Thomas O'Keefe, Mar 16, 2026)
observations.notes: Summit Creek Bridge (on the AW section above) to Icehouse: '21 miles ... in 3 hours, a pace of 7 miles per hour'. It covers all of leidl-icehouse plus about 5 mi upstream, so it is not a catalog section. Craft is not stated on the reach page (filed as raft). High water: 'up into the trees ... eddies were limited'. The USGS daily mean for 2026-03-16 is 4570 (provisional).

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Icehouse to Turkey Hole' (Thomas O'Keefe, Apr 1, 2024)
observations.notes: Source: 'The float time was 2 hours.' Party of three, craft not stated. The report's 'Gauge Reading' field says 2300 CFS ('Medium Runnable'). Batch 1 (2026-10-25) replaced the USGS daily mean of 2120 that was used before the report page was found; the daily mean is kept here for reference.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Family float from Upper Pitt Boat Ramp to 5 Mile Boat Ramp' (Eric Porter, Aug 30, 2025)
observations.notes: Upper Pitt to 5 Mile Ramp is not a catalog section and the distance is not stated. Mixed craft: 12' rafts, IKs, SUP and an inflatable canoe, with children. Source: 'about 2 hours with some stops and relaxed pace' at '~750 cfs'. The USGS daily mean is 735.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Between Two Hatcheries' (Sam Westover, Mar 9, 2025)
observations.notes: Two canoes and two kayaks. Source: 'just under 2 hours, including a 20 minute lunch stop', with a 'strong headwind'. The reporter mentions AW's 5000 cfs upper limit but gives no flow. flowCfs is the USGS daily mean for tripDate (approved unless noted), not an instantaneous reading; the source gives no flow. Note that the v1 refSpeedBasis ('under 2 hr at ~2,400 cfs') wrongly combined this report's time with the Aug 2025 report's flow.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report (J F, Jun 2024)
observations.notes: Packraft, Salmon Hatchery to I-5, '(21/22 miles) in about 4 hours'. The date is the report header date and the trip date is uncertain. Not a catalog section. The reporter's rule of thumb was 'about 1mph per 1000cfs'. flowCfs is the USGS daily mean for tripDate (approved unless noted), not an instantaneous reading; the source gives no flow.

observations.sourceName: CowlitzKayak.com 'Places to Paddle' (outfitter)
observations.notes: Outfitter guidance, not a dated trip: Barrier Dam Boat Launch to Blue Creek Boat Launch 'Average Time ... 2 Hours'. No flow is given.

observations.sourceName: KATU AM Northwest: 'Local River Floats to Cool Off!' (guidebook author Adam Sawyer, Jul 6, 2021)
observations.notes: Guidebook-author estimate, not a dated trip: Tacoma Power Barrier Dam Boat Launch to Blue Creek Boat Ramp, 'Estimated Float Time: 1-2 hours', framed for summer tubing/family floats. elapsedMinutes is null because the source gives a 60-120 min range (3.75-7.5 mph over 7.5 mi). No flow is given. Added in batch 1 (2026-10-25).

observations.sourceName: NPS Hanford: Paddle the Hanford Reach (agency guide)
observations.notes: Agency guide, not a dated trip: about 19 mi and 'typically takes 4-6 hours, but this can vary dramatically due to winds and water levels'. 'A moderate trip would have flows of 80,000 to 120,000' cfs. elapsedMinutes is null because the source gives a 240-360 min range.

observations.sourceName: Andrew's Adventure Notes: Hanford Reach (trip notes)
observations.notes: Sea kayaks. Source: '4.5 hours at 111 kcfs ... (not including time spent stopping for lunch)', 'pretty casual', with drifting from the White Bluffs to the launch. No trip date is given.

observations.sourceName: Andrew's Adventure Notes: Hanford Reach (trip notes)
observations.notes: Sea kayaks. Source: 'a mere 2.5 hrs at 170 kcfs (not including time spent stopping for lunch)'. No trip date is given.

observations.sourceName: Wenatchee Outdoors: Columbia-Hanford Reach (Dave and Jerry Jaecks, posted May 15, 2016)
observations.notes: Source: 'Our time: 2hours, 50 minutes', in 'NO wind and a BRISK current'. Kayaks. The trip date is not stated beyond the post date and no flow is given.

observations.sourceName: Jay's Kayak Trip Log: Hanford Reach June 1 2008
observations.notes: Sea kayaks. On the water 11:05, off 15:50 (local). That includes repeated play runs at Coyote Rapids, a lunch stop and a late headwind. GPS logged 18.4 nm (about 21.2 statute mi). The reporter said 'appr 200,000 cfs' and the USGS daily mean is 220000. Stop time is not quantified.

observations.sourceName: Incoherence blog trip report: Kayaking the Skagit River between Marblemount and Rockport (Jan 14, 2018)
observations.notes: Sea kayaks. Source: 'Run duration: 1:55 (averaged 6.5 knots, mostly drifting)', 'Run length: 10.5 miles', 'appx. 9700 cfs'. The USGS daily mean at 12181000 is 8380. The catalog section is 10.4 mi.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Sauk River - Darrington to Skagit confluence' (Jake Risken, Jun 26, 2022)
observations.notes: Sauk Prairie Bridge to Faber Ferry North (on the Skagit), about 23 mi. That covers both catalog Sauk sections plus the Skagit, so it is not a catalog section. Source: 'On-river time was 6 hours (inclusive of a quick lunch break)' and 'between 8000 cfs and 9000 cfs I think' (8500 is the midpoint). The USGS daily mean at 12189500 is 10400.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report (Ariel Leigh, Jul 22, 2020)
observations.notes: SUPs from Government Bridge to Faber South on the Skagit. This is below the catalog sections and the distance is not stated. Source: 'River time was 2.5 hours' at '4530cfs'. The reporter did not say which gauge.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report (Michael Zlatkovsky, Apr 2015)
observations.notes: Packrafts from Railroad Bridge (2.5 mi above Big Eddy) to the Sultan River confluence, '~10 miles' in '3.5 hours'. This covers about 2.5 mi above Big Eddy plus most or all of big-eddy-sultan. Source: 'paddling most of the time'. Flow 2950 is reported and the USGS daily mean is 2910.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Harlequin Duck Survey' (Thomas O'Keefe, May 18, 2024)
observations.notes: 'just over 2 hours for the full Upper Middle run from the Taylor River down to Granite Creek' (125 is approximate). The put-in is the Taylor River confluence, not catalog Bridge View, and AW reach length was not recorded. Survey pace. flowCfs is the USGS daily mean for tripDate (approved unless noted), not an instantaneous reading; the source gives no flow.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Harlequin Duck Survey' (Thomas O'Keefe, Apr 27, 2024)
observations.notes: Kayaks and a raft. Source: 'approximately 2.5 hours on the Upper Middle and 2 hours on the Middle Middle for total run of approximately 5 hours that included a break for lunch'. This is a wildlife survey, so it is slow. flowCfs is the USGS daily mean for tripDate (approved unless noted), not an instantaneous reading; the source gives no flow.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Untitled' (Dec 12, 2021)
observations.notes: Hardshell kayaks from the concrete bridge 'to the power lines in Tanner'. Source: 'approximately 2 hours with the quick stop to scout' at 'just under 5k ... peaked around 5200'. The USGS daily mean at 12141300 is 2070, so the reporter probably used a different gauge. Treat the flow as uncertain.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Great run! Perfect water level' (Valea Lund, May 13, 2023)
observations.notes: Flaming Geyser Park to Porter Levee Natural Area (before the Hwy 18 bridge), which runs past the catalog Whitney Bridge take-out. Distance is not stated. Source: 'Took 3 hours with just one portage'. flowCfs is the USGS daily mean for tripDate (approved unless noted), not an instantaneous reading; the source gives no flow.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report (Ariel Leigh, Jul 22, 2020)
observations.notes: SUPs from Lake Wenatchee to Plain on 7/17/2020. Source: '2 hours on the river' at 'Flow was 2600cfs'. The USGS daily mean at 12457000 is 2580. Distance is the catalog length. Wind is noted as typical.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Lower Methow Packraft Trip' (Scott Harding, Jun 28, 2022)
observations.notes: Solo decked packraft, McFarland Creek access to the Douglas County PUD access about 3/4 mi above Hwy 97. Source: 'about 2-1/2 hours--pretty quick at this flow' for '17 river miles'. flowCfs is the USGS daily mean for tripDate (approved unless noted), not an instantaneous reading; the source gives no flow.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Averill to Burma Rd. bridge- packrafters' (Nick Cher, Apr 16, 2026)
observations.notes: Packrafts, Averill to Burma Rd bridge, a part of averill-pateros. Source: 'ran this 8.4 mile section in 75 minutes' at '4310 CFS' (Pateros gauge). The USGS daily mean is 4270.

observations.sourceName: Yakima River Tubing: How It Works (outfitter)
observations.notes: Outfitter guidance for tubes from Umtanum to Roza, 10.9 mi (umtanum-lmuma + lmuma-roza): 'Float time: 3hrs - 4 hours'. Not a dated trip and no flow is given. elapsedMinutes is null because the source gives a range.

observations.sourceName: Triad River Tours: Skagit River Rafting Trip Summary (outfitter, NPS special-use permittee)
observations.notes: Outfitter guidance, not a dated trip: 'Length of trip: 9 miles. Duration of trip: 2-2.5 hours on the river depending on river flow.' Its sample itinerary is 'Rafting on the river' 10:15am-12:15pm for '8 miles'. elapsedMinutes is null because the source gives a 120-150 min range (about 3.6-4.5 mph over 8.9 mi). No flow is given; the season is May-September (dam-regulated). Added in the final run.

observations.sourceName: American Whitewater trip report: 'Beautiful Day on the Green River Gorge' (Thomas O'Keefe, Mar 31, 2026)
observations.notes: Full Green River Gorge run. Source: ready to launch at Kanaskat Palmer at 'noon', 'reached Paradise at 1:30pm', picked up another boater, a lunch break in a sunny spot, and 'at the take-out around 3:00pm'. So about 180 min including an unquantified pickup and lunch break (about 4.0 mph gross). Craft not stated (filed as kayak). flowCfs is the USGS daily mean for tripDate (approved unless noted), not an instantaneous reading; the source gives no flow. Value 1250 is provisional. Added in the final run.

observations.sourceName: The Mountaineers trip report: 'Grande Ronde River' (Logan DeGrand, Jun 9, 2024; trip Jun 6-8, 2024)
observations.notes: Packrafts, Minam to Boggan's Oasis (66 mi) over 3 days, which includes Troy-Boggans. Source: 'With 6,500 CFS pushing us along, our average speed was 6.5 mph'; 'The gauge at Troy was between 5,800 - 6,500 CFS'; '22 miles took barely 4 hours of paddling' (day 1, above Troy); from RM 58 Troy was 'only 2 hours away at this flow'. Not a catalog section, so elapsedMinutes is null; flowCfs is the midpoint of the reporter's range. Added in the final run.

observations.sourceName: 'Float Time Estimates on the Wallowa and Grande Ronde Wild and Scenic Rivers' (handout, apparently BLM-referenced; read from a search-index excerpt, the PDF returned HTTP 402)
observations.notes: Not a dated trip. The excerpt gives Troy to Boggan's Oasis 19 mi and Troy to Heller Bar 45 mi, and a speed table keyed to cfs at Troy: under 1,000 '0 to 1 mph'; 1,000-2,000 '1 to 2 mph'; 2,000-6,000 '2 to 4 mph'; 6,000-10,000 '4 to 5 mph'; over 10,000 '5 mph +'. Author not confirmed and full document not opened, so low confidence. Applies to both grande-ronde-troy and grande-ronde-lower. Added in the final run.

observations.sourceName: 'Float Time Estimates on the Wallowa and Grande Ronde Wild and Scenic Rivers' (handout, apparently BLM-referenced; read from a search-index excerpt, the PDF returned HTTP 402)
observations.notes: Same source as the grande-ronde-troy entry: Troy to Heller Bar '45' mi (catalog troy-heller-bar is 46.2), with the cfs-at-Troy speed table (2,000-6,000 cfs '2 to 4 mph'; 6,000-10,000 '4 to 5 mph'). Not a dated trip, low confidence. Added in the final run.

observations.sourceName: River Rider: Tubing (outfitter)
observations.notes: Outfitter guidance, not a dated trip: 'Leavenworth to Peshastin, Class I 2 miles - 1.5 hours, July - August', open only once the Wenatchee drops to 'around 900 CFS'. This is the outfitter's 2-mile tube run from its east-Leavenworth base, not the 5.2-mile catalog leavenworth-peshastin section, so sectionId is null. Tubes at low summer flow (about 1.3 mph); not used for refSpeedMph. Added in the final run.

observations.sourceName: PDX Rafting: White Salmon River Rafting (outfitter)
observations.notes: Outfitter guidance, not a dated trip: half-day 'Distance: 8 miles Time on River: ~2 hours' starting at BZ Corner, which runs past Husum Falls (run or portaged) into the Lower White Salmon, so it is not the 4.4-mile catalog bz-husum section. Full-day 15 miles '~4 hours' including lunch. About 4 mph gross. No flow is given. Added in the final run.
